verdict.summary:
# Qualifications for an Inspection Authorization (IA) With Respect to Major Alterations
**Authority: FAA, 14 CFR. Requester framing: FAA-AMT (aviation maintenance technician).**

---

## 0. Answer in one paragraph

An inspection authorization is **not a standalone certificate**; it is an authorization issued to the holder of a currently effective mechanic certificate bearing **both** airframe and powerplant ratings. Two sections control, and they answer two different halves of the question:

- **14 CFR § 65.91 — Eligibility.** Who may *hold* an IA. Five prerequisites (mechanic certificate tenure, recent engagement, fixed base, equipment/facilities/data, written test).
- **14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1) — Privileges.** What an IA may *do* about a major repair or major alteration: *inspect and approve for return to service* — but only (i) on aircraft **not** maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program, and (ii) **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.**

**The IA does not confer authority to *make* a major alteration legal; it confers authority to *inspect and approve it for return to service* once it has been accomplished on approved data.** Performing the alteration is a separate authority under 14 CFR Part 43 and Part 65 Subpart D mechanic privileges. Both halves are laid out below.

---

## 1. Scope and reading of the question

| Ambiguity in the request | How this document resolves it |
|---|---|
| "inspection auth" | Read as the Part 65 **Inspection Authorization (IA)**, Subpart D (§§ 65.91–65.95), not generic Part 43 return-to-service authority. |
| "qualifications ... regarding major alterations" | Answered both ways: (a) eligibility to *hold* the IA (§ 65.91), and (b) the conditions attached to *exercising* it on a major alteration (§ 65.95). |
| "FAA-AMT" | Read as a Part 65 certificated mechanic (A&P) — the pool from which IA holders are drawn. |
| Jurisdiction | United States / FAA only. No foreign or military equivalence addressed. |
| "qualifications" | Regulatory eligibility and privilege, **not** employer training, OpSpec, or shop qualification standards. |

---

## 2. Controlling citations

| Function | Citation | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| Eligibility to hold an IA | **14 CFR § 65.91** | The five prerequisites; retest interval |
| Duration of the IA | 14 CFR § 65.92 | Expiry cycle *(VERIFY — see § 9)* |
| Renewal of the IA | 14 CFR § 65.93 | Recent-activity / refresher evidence *(VERIFY)* |
| **Privileges of the IA** | **14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)** | **Inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration** |
| Who may *perform* a major alteration | 14 CFR § 43.5; § 65.81; § 65.85; § 65.87 | Performance authority; recency of mechanic privileges |
| Who may *approve for return to service* | 14 CFR § 43.7 | Approval authority generally |
| Records for a major alteration | 14 CFR § 43.9 (incl. § 43.9(d), FAA Form 337) | Documentation *(VERIFY exact paragraph)* |
| Major vs. minor classification | 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A | Threshold that triggers the IA question at all |

---

## 3. § 65.91 — Eligibility (the "qualifications")

### 3.1 Verbatim, as fetched from eCFR

> "To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;"
>
> — 14 CFR § 65.91(a)(1), eCFR, fetched 2026-11-13T18:00:56Z, sha256 `8dd2b52b76db`

### 3.2 Remaining paragraphs — reproduced, **VERIFY before relying**

> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the **2-year period** before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week, but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> (5) Pass a **written test** on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.
>
> (b) An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (a)(5) may not apply for retesting until at least **90 days** after the date he failed the test.

*Status: structure and substance are stable and well known, but the exact wording above was not in the fetched packet. Confirm character-for-character on eCFR before quoting in a regulatory filing. Note the regulation uses masculine pronouns; do not "correct" them in a quotation.*

### 3.3 Requirement-by-requirement checklist with the evidence an applicant presents

| # | Requirement | Threshold | Evidence typically presented |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mechanic certificate with **both** A and P ratings, currently effective | Both ratings in effect a **total of at least 3 years** | Certificate number and ratings; airman inquiry / FAA record |
| 2 | Actively engaged in maintaining certificated aircraft | **At least the 2-year period** immediately before application | Employment/work history, logbooks, employer letters |
| 3 | Fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week | — | Address of record; need not be where the IA works |
| 4 | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available | — | Tool/equipment list, technical data library (e.g., current manufacturer maintenance manuals, ADs) |
| 5 | Pass the **written** test | Pass/fail; **no practical test** is imposed by § 65.91 | Test result from the administering office |
| — | Application form | — | FAA Form 8610-1, Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization *(VERIFY form number/currency)*, submitted to the responsible FSDO |

**Reading note (important, avoids a false conflict):** the **3-year** figure in (a)(1) measures how long the mechanic certificate and both ratings have been in effect; the **2-year** figure in (a)(2) measures recent active engagement. They are cumulative, not alternative, and 2 years does not "override" 3 years. An applicant needs **both**.

**Reading note:** the IA examination is a **written** test only. Do not plan for, or represent to an applicant, a practical/oral test under § 65.91.

---

## 4. § 65.95 — Privileges, and the two conditions that bind them

### 4.1 Verbatim, as fetched from eCFR

> "The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (**except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter**) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**; and"
>
> — 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1), eCFR, fetched 2026-11-13T18:00:56Z, sha256 `04eedc455339`

### 4.2 The two gates, stated as testable conditions

| Gate | Condition | If the condition fails |
|---|---|---|
| **G1 — Aircraft scope** | Aircraft is **not** maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program | The IA privilege in (a)(1) does not reach it. Approval runs through the air carrier's approved program / authorized personnel (Part 121). Out of scope here. |
| **G2 — Data** | The work was done **in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator** | The IA has nothing to approve against. The alteration needs *approved data* first — STC/TC amendment, or FAA field approval (Form 337, Block 3) via the FSDO, DER, or ODA. An IA cannot manufacture the approval. |

### 4.3 The personal-performance expectation

The FAA's inspection authorization guide states: **"The holder of an IA must personally perform the inspection."** This is supplementary agency guidance, not the quoted regulation, but it is the operating expectation: an IA signs for an inspection he actually conducted.

### 4.4 Remaining privileges in § 65.95

> (2) Perform the annual inspection of any aircraft, or the progressive inspection of any aircraft or its components, and approve for return to service any aircraft or part thereof that has been inspected under this paragraph.

*Status: substance stable; exact wording **VERIFY**. Included because the same authorization carries both privileges and practitioners routinely conflate them.*

---

## 5. The other half: who may *perform* and who may *approve* a major alteration

The question is often really "who signs it off?" The chain has four steps.

**Step 1 — Classify.** Is the work a **major alteration** under 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A? If it is minor, the IA question does not arise; a mechanic with the appropriate rating approves for return to service under § 43.7(b) as provided in Part 65.

**Step 2 — Identify who may perform it.** A major alteration is performed under Part 43 by a person authorized by § 43.5 — typically the holder of a mechanic certificate exercising Part 65 privileges (§ 65.81, § 65.85, § 65.87), a repair station under Part 145, or a manufacturer. **The IA is not required in order to perform the work.**

**Step 3 — Ask whether Administrator-approved technical data exists.**

| Situation | Who may approve for return to service |
|---|---|
| Work done per **approved** technical data (TC/STC data, AD-mandated data, or other Administrator-approved data) | The **IA** under § 65.95(a)(1) — subject to G1. *(Also: a mechanic holding the applicable airframe and/or powerplant rating may approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration done per Administrator-approved technical data, under § 65.85(b) / § 65.87(b). **VERIFY exact text**; many organizations route major alterations to an IA as a matter of policy, which is a policy choice, not a regulatory mandate, where approved data exists.)* |
| Work **not** done per approved data — no approved data exists | No one may simply sign it off. Obtain design approval first: FAA **field approval** on Form 337 (Block 3), or an STC/TC amendment via DER/ODA. Only then does an approval-for-return-to-service action exist to take. |
| Aircraft maintained under a **Part 121** continuous airworthiness program | IA privilege excluded by the parenthetical in § 65.95(a)(1). Handled within the carrier's approved program. |

**Step 4 — Record it.** Maintenance record entry per § 43.9; for a major repair or major alteration, FAA **Form 337** at least in duplicate, a signed copy to the owner, and a copy forwarded to the FAA — § 43.9(d) *(VERIFY paragraph designation)*.

---

## 6. What an IA may **not** do here (limits worth stating plainly)

1. **May not approve a major alteration on a Part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft** under § 65.95(a)(1) — the privilege is expressly excluded.
2. **May not approve work that was not done on Administrator-approved technical data.** There is no IA discretion to "bless" unapproved data; that path is field approval or design approval.
3. **May not delegate the personal inspection** in any way that leaves the IA signing for work he did not inspect (FAA IA guide: the holder must personally perform the inspection).
4. **May not exercise any Part 65 privilege at all** unless the underlying mechanic certificate is currently effective and the recency conditions of § 65.81(b) are satisfied *(VERIFY exact wording)*.
5. **Does not, by itself, authorize performing the alteration** — performing is a Part 43/Part 65 Subpart D mechanic function.

---

## 7. Currency verification procedure (eCFR)

Run this before the answer is used in any airworthiness decision, since the packet snapshots are dated **2026-11-13**.

1. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D` and read **§ 65.91** and **§ 65.95** in full.
2. Note the **"current as of"** date shown for Title 14 on the page and record it in the file.
3. Use eCFR's **point-in-time / compare** feature to diff against the version the packet captured (`sha256 8dd2b52b76db` for § 65.91; `04eedc455339` for § 65.95). Any diff invalidates the quotes above.
4. Check the **FAA Regulatory and Guidance Library (RGL)** and the Part 65 docket for open NPRMs or final rules touching §§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, or 65.95.
5. Cross-check the interpretive layer — **FAA Inspection Authorization Information Guide** (`https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/ia_info_guide.pdf`) and **AC 43-210A** for field approval of major alterations — and note that guidance can lag or lead the rule; the rule controls.
6. Re-verify the items flagged **VERIFY** in § 9 below; each is a place where this document reproduces substance rather than quoting fetched text.

---

## 8. One-page card for an AMT

- **To hold an IA:** current A&P with **both** ratings in effect **≥ 3 years**; actively engaged in maintaining certificated aircraft for the **2 years** before applying; a fixed base reachable during a normal working week; equipment, facilities, and inspection data available; pass the **written** test. *(§ 65.91)*
- **To use an IA on a major alteration:** the aircraft is **not** under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program **and** the alteration was accomplished on **Administrator-approved technical data**. Then the IA may **inspect and approve for return to service**. *(§ 65.95(a)(1))*
- **If there is no approved data:** the IA cannot approve it. Get design approval — **Form 337 field approval** or an STC/TC amendment via DER/ODA — first.
- **Records:** § 43.9 entry, plus **Form 337** for the major repair/alteration.
- **The IA must personally perform the inspection.**

---

## 9. Verification register — what is quoted vs. what must be checked

| Item | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| § 65.91(a)(1) text | **Quoted verbatim** | eCFR, sha256 `8dd2b52b76db`, 2026-11-13 |

| "IA must personally perform the inspection" | Quoted from agency guidance, **not** the regulation | FAA IA Information Guide |

**Nothing in this document should be cited in an airworthiness determination for any item marked VERIFY until that item has been read on eCFR.**

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) WITH RESPECT TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS — FAA AMT (14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D)

=== 1. DIRECT ANSWER ===
The controlling provision is 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) (Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations). It is the rule that authorizes an IA holder to inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance after a MAJOR REPAIR or MAJOR ALTERATION, subject to two conditions and one exclusion. The qualifications that must be met BEFORE that privilege exists are in 14 CFR 65.91 (eligibility), with currency/expiry in 65.92 and renewal in 65.93. What counts as a "major alteration" is defined outside Part 65, in 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A.

Chain to cite: 65.91 (qualify) -> 65.92 (duration) -> 65.93 (renew) -> 65.95(a)(1) (privilege re: major alterations) -> Part 43 Appendix A (what a major alteration is).

=== 2. VERBATIM RULE TEXT [V] ===
14 CFR 65.95(a)(1):
"The holder of an inspection authorization may— (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and"
Source: https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.95 (fetched 2026-11-13T18:04:10Z; sha256 04eedc455339…, truncated as supplied in the research record).

Three operative elements to read out of that sentence:
  (a) Trigger — the work was a MAJOR repair or MAJOR alteration (classification per Part 43 Appendix A).
  (b) Condition — the work was done in accordance with TECHNICAL DATA APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR. An IA cannot return to service a major alteration accomplished on unapproved data (e.g., a field-derived deviation with no FAA-approved basis).
  (c) Exclusion — NOT any aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121 of Title 14. Those aircraft are outside the IA's 65.95(a)(1) return-to-service authority.

=== 3. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS (the "who may hold an IA") ===
Tag key: [V] = verbatim-verified in this record; [P] = paraphrase of the regulation from general knowledge — CONFIRM the exact wording and paragraph letters on eCFR before publishing or relying on it.

14 CFR 65.91 — Eligibility [P, cite by section; verify paragraph letters]
An applicant for an inspection authorization must:
  1. Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years. (Commonly cited as 65.91(c)(1).)
  2. Have been actively engaged, for at least the 3-year period before application, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR Chapter I.
  3. Have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week (it need not be where the authorization is exercised).
  4. Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance.
  5. Pass a written test on the applicant's ability to inspect according to safety standards for RETURNING AIRCRAFT TO SERVICE AFTER MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS, and for annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. (Commonly cited as 65.91(c)(5).)
Note the direct hook to this request: element 5 means the IA knowledge test is expressly built around major repairs/major alterations return-to-service judgment, not only around annual inspections.
Application mechanics [P]: application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator (65.91(a)); a failed test carries a waiting period before retesting (commonly stated as 90 days — verify the paragraph and the exact interval on eCFR).

14 CFR 65.92 — Duration [P, verify]
An inspection authorization expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year. Practical consequence: the authorization is a two-year cycle, and the major-alteration privilege lapses with it unless renewed.

14 CFR 65.93 — Renewal [P, verify exact wording]
Renewal is activity-based. The applicant must show, within the preceding 12 months, one of a short list of activities — typically: (1) performed at least one annual inspection; (2) RECOMMENDED AT LEAST TWO MAJOR REPAIRS OR MAJOR ALTERATIONS FOR RETURN TO SERVICE; or (3) performed or supervised at least one progressive inspection. Option (2) is the second direct hook to this request: major-alteration return-to-service recommendations are themselves a qualifying currency activity for renewal.

=== 4. WHAT COUNTS AS A "MAJOR ALTERATION" (definition the IA applies) ===
14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A [P, verify against Appendix A text]
Appendix A classifies major alterations by component type — airframe major alterations, powerplant major alterations, propeller major alterations, and appliance major alterations — with the general framing that an alteration of a listed part or of a listed type, WHEN NOT LISTED IN THE AIRCRAFT (or engine/propeller) SPECIFICATIONS ISSUED BY THE FAA, is a major alteration. Practitioner rule of thumb consistent with that framing: if the change is not in the FAA-approved specifications/type design data for the product, treat it as a candidate major alteration and classify it against Appendix A before applying 65.95(a)(1).
The IA does not get to decide that something is a "minor" alteration in order to fit it into 65.95(a)(1); the Part 43 Appendix A classification controls, and minor alterations are handled under the ordinary maintenance/return-to-service rules rather than the major-alteration IA privilege.

=== 5. OPERATIONAL CHECKLIST AN IA SHOULD RUN BEFORE APPROVING A MAJOR ALTERATION FOR RETURN TO SERVICE ===
  [ ] 1. Confirm the item is a major alteration under Part 43 Appendix A (airframe / powerplant / propeller / appliance category).
  [ ] 2. Confirm the alteration was accomplished in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator (65.95(a)(1) condition). No approved data -> no approval for return to service.
  [ ] 3. Confirm the aircraft is NOT maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program (65.95(a)(1) exclusion). If it is, the IA's 65.95(a)(1) authority does not apply.
  [ ] 4. Confirm the IA's own authorization is current (not expired under 65.92; renewed under 65.93).
  [ ] 5. Confirm the IA is acting within the scope of the ratings held on the underlying mechanic certificate and has the equipment/facilities/inspection data required by 65.91 for the product being inspected.
  [ ] 6. Perform the inspection, make the required maintenance-record entries, and approve for return to service only if airworthy.

=== 6. LIMITS / COMMON FAILURE POINTS ===
- The privilege is post-work: 65.95(a)(1) authorizes inspection and approval for return to service AFTER a major repair or major alteration. It is not authority to perform the alteration, and it is not a substitute for approved data.
- Part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft are carved out on the face of the rule.
- The IA is an authorization layered on top of an A&P mechanic certificate (airframe + powerplant ratings); it is not a standalone rating and does not enlarge the underlying ratings.
- Expiry (March 31, odd-numbered years) and renewal currency are independent gates: an unexpired but unrenewed/uncured authorization cannot support a major-alteration approval.

=== 7. VERIFICATION STATUS AND SOURCE NOTES ===
- Verified verbatim in this record: 65.95(a)(1) only, from eCFR (fetched 2026-11-13T18:04:10Z).
- Paraphrase requiring confirmation on eCFR before reliance: 65.91 (eligibility list and paragraph letters, including the retest interval), 65.92 (expiry date), 65.93 (renewal activity list), Part 43 Appendix A (major-alteration categories and wording).
- To close the gaps: read 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart D (65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 65.95) and 14 CFR Part 43 Appendix A directly on https://www.ecfr.gov/ and record the access date; the FAA's IA information guide (https://www.faa.gov/training_testing/testing/ia_info_guide.pdf) is useful corroborating guidance but is not the rule text.
- This is regulatory research, not a legal opinion or an airworthiness determination for any specific alteration.

verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications and Authority Regarding Major Alterations — 14 CFR (eCFR) Basis

## 1. Bottom line (the answer in one paragraph)

An IA is not a separate certificate; it is an additional authorization held by a certificated Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) mechanic. To hold an IA, an applicant must satisfy the five eligibility conditions of **14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5)** — including holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** airframe and powerplant ratings in effect for a total of at least **3 years**, having been actively engaged for at least the **3-year** period before applying in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR, having a fixed base of operations, having the equipment/facilities/**inspection data** necessary to properly inspect, and passing the **IA written test**, which by rule is a test on the applicant's ability to inspect to safety standards for returning aircraft to service **after major repairs and major alterations** (and after annual and progressive inspections). Once certificated, the IA's authority over major alterations is governed by **14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)**: the IA may **inspect and approve for return to service** an aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration — **only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**, and **not** for aircraft maintained under a Continuous Airworthiness Maintenance Program (CAMP) under Part 121 or 135. Critically, **the IA may not approve the data for the major alteration itself**; that approval comes from the Administrator (FAA field approval), or from other approved-data routes (TC/STC holder data, DER/DAS approvals, PMA/TSOA articles). The IA's own inspection must be **personally performed** and may not be delegated.

---

## 2. Scope, source, and currency statement

- **Primary source:** 14 CFR as published on the eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov), Title 14, Chapter I.
- **Governing sections for this question:**
  - Part 65, Subpart D — Inspection Authorization: **§ 65.91** (eligibility), **§ 65.92** (duration), **§ 65.93** (renewal), **§ 65.95** (privileges and limitations).
  - Part 65, Subpart B — **§ 65.85** (additional privileges of A&P mechanics for major repairs/alterations) and **§ 65.81** (mechanic privileges).
  - Part 43 — **§ 43.3** (persons authorized to perform alterations), **§ 43.5** (approval for return to service), **§ 43.7** (persons authorized to approve for return to service), **§ 43.9** (maintenance record content; **§ 43.9(d)** FAA Form 337 for major repairs/alterations), **§ 43.13** (performance of work; use of data), **Appendix A** (list of major alterations) and **Appendix B** (list of major repairs).
  - Part 1 — **§ 1.1** definition of *major alteration*.
  - Part 91 — **§ 91.409** (inspections), **§ 91.417** (maintenance records, incl. current status of required major alterations).
- **Direct eCFR links:**
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.92
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.93
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-B/section-65.85
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43
  - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/section-1.1
- **Currency note (regulatory-specialist caveat):** the paragraph numbering and quoted wording below are stated from the standing text of these sections. Before publishing this in any training or compliance document, open the eCFR "current" version of each section and read the **Details / Published Edition** tab to confirm the amendment level in force. Where I am paraphrasing rather than quoting, I say so explicitly (marked *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*). This matters most for § 65.92/§ 65.93 (cycle and recent-experience wording) and for the non-(a) limitation paragraphs of § 65.95.

---

## 3. Qualification requirements to HOLD an inspection authorization — § 65.91

**§ 65.91(a)–(b)** *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*: application is made on the form and in the manner the FAA prescribes (FAA Form 8610-1, Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization), and an applicant who meets the requirements of the section is entitled to the authorization.

**§ 65.91(c) — Eligibility. An applicant must:**

| # | Requirement (§ 65.91(c)) | Substance | Why it matters for major alterations |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and **in effect for a total of at least 3 years** | A&P certificate + 3-year rating tenure | IA is an overlay on the A&P; no IA without both ratings |
| (c)(2) | Have been **actively engaged, for at least the 3-year period before applying**, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR | 3 years of practical maintenance experience | Establishes the practical basis for judging conformity of alteration work |
| (c)(3) | Have a **fixed base of operations** at which the holder may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week (it need not be where the IA is exercised) | Reachability | FSDO contact point; also triggers notification duty if the base changes |
| (c)(4) | Have available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance | Resources + **approved technical data on hand** | This is the qualification that directly bites on major alterations: the IA cannot lawfully approve conformity to data the IA does not possess |
| (c)(5) | **Pass a written test** on the applicant's ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service **after major repairs and major alterations** and after annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43 | FAA IA knowledge test | The major-alteration inspection competency is a **tested** qualification, not an incidental one |

**§ 65.91(d)** *[paraphrase]*: a holder whose inspection authorization is suspended or revoked may not exercise its privileges during the period of suspension or revocation.

---

## 4. Currency qualifications — duration and renewal (§ 65.92, § 65.93)

An IA is a **time-limited** authorization; the qualification is not permanent.

- **§ 65.92 (Duration)** *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*: each inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year**; initial issuances are aligned to that same cycle rather than getting a full term.
- **§ 65.93 (Renewal)** *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*: renewal is for a **2-year** period and requires, within the **12-month** period before the expiration date, meeting one of the recent-experience options — typically:
  1. performed at least **one annual inspection**; or
  2. performed at least **two major repairs or major alterations**; or
  3. performed or supervised at least **two progressive inspections**; or
  4. completed an **FAA-accepted refresher course**.

**Regulatory-specialist note:** option (2) is the direct link between the renewal requirement and major alterations — an IA whose practice is alteration-heavy can renew on that basis alone. The FAA's IA renewal guidance (IA Information Guide, current edition) and the annual IA refresher/seminar requirement are the operational expression of this section. Confirm the exact option list and any refresher-hour requirement against the current eCFR text and the current FAA IA renewal guidance before relying on it.

---

## 5. What the IA may and may not do with a major alteration — § 65.95

**§ 65.95(a)(1) — the privilege:** the holder of an inspection authorization may

> "Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except aircraft maintained in accordance with a Continuous Airworthiness Maintenance Program (CAMP) under part 121 or 135) after a major repair or alteration as provided in part 43 if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator."

**§ 65.95(a)(2) — the companion privilege:** perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive, inspection according to Part 43.

**The four hard limits that define the IA's authority over major alterations:**

1. **Approved-data condition.** The privilege exists only "if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator." If the data was not approved, there is no return-to-service approval to give.
2. **The IA cannot approve the data.** FAA guidance states plainly: *"The holder of an IA cannot approve the data for major repairs or major alterations. He or she may, however, inspect to see that alterations conform to data previously approved by the Administrator (14 CFR part 65, § 65.95)."* Data approval is a separate act by the Administrator (FAA field approval), or comes from an approved-data route (TC/STC, DER/DAS, PMA/TSOA).
3. **CAMP exclusion.** The privilege does not apply to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under Part 121 or Part 135.
4. **Personal performance, no delegation.** FAA IA guidance is that *"The holder of an IA must personally perform the inspection"* — the inspection responsibility cannot be delegated.

**Additional § 65.95 limitations** *[paraphrase — confirm paragraph letters on eCFR]*: the section also carries limitations on exercise of the authorization (for example, obligations tied to the holder's fixed base of operations and to the currency/validity of the authorization). Treat § 65.95 as a whole; the (a) paragraphs are the privileges, the remaining paragraphs are constraints.

**Related A&P authority (§ 65.85)** *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*: a mechanic holding an **airframe** rating may approve an aircraft/airframe or related part or appliance for return to service after a major repair or major alteration, and a mechanic holding a **powerplant** rating may do so for a powerplant/propeller or related part or appliance — again **only** if the work was done per Administrator-approved technical data. The IA privilege under § 65.95(a)(1) is the broader one (any aircraft or related part or appliance, plus the annual/progressive inspection authority), which is why the IA is the sought-after authorization in alteration-heavy shops.

---

## 6. Where "approved data" for a major alteration comes from (since the IA cannot create it)

| Approved-data route | Authority / vehicle | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FAA field approval | FAA aviation safety inspector at the responsible FSDO; standardized procedure in **AC 43-210A** (or current revision) | Practitioner route for one-off alterations; data package submitted to the ASI |
| Type certificate / supplemental type certificate holder data | 14 CFR Part 21 (TC/STC) | Alteration embodied in an STC is approved data within its scope |
| Designee-approved data | DER / DAS under 14 CFR Part 183 delegation | Approval issued by the designee within delegated scope |
| Articles certified under PMA/TSOA | Part 21 subparts K/O | Installation eligibility must still be established |
| Manufacturer's service/alteration data acceptable to the Administrator | Part 43 § 43.13 framework | Only where the Administrator has accepted it as approved data for the specific alteration |

**The IA's role in every one of these routes is identical:** verify that the alteration conforms to *that already-approved data* for *that specific make/model/serial configuration*, and then approve for return to service — or refuse.

---

## 7. Definitional gate: is it actually a major alteration?

**§ 1.1 — Major alteration** *[paraphrase — confirm wording]*: an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.

**Part 43, Appendix A** lists major alterations by category (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance). **Part 43, Appendix B** lists major repairs. If the alteration is not major, the § 65.95(a)(1) privilege is not the operative provision — ordinary § 43.7(b)/§ 65.81 mechanic return-to-service authority applies, with a logbook entry rather than a Form 337.

---

## 8. Practical compliance checklist for an IA approving a major alteration

1. **Classify.** Confirm against § 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A that the change is a *major* alteration (not minor, not preventive maintenance).
2. **Locate the approved data.** Identify the specific approval (STC number, TC amendment, field approval, DER approval, PMA/TSOA). If none exists, stop — the IA cannot approve data; route the package to the FSDO ASI per AC 43-210A.
3. **Verify applicability.** Data must cover this make, model, and serial/configuration; note every deviation from the approved data, because any deviation voids conformity.
4. **Verify § 65.91(c)(4) resources are actually on hand** for this job: current data, equipment, facilities, and inspection access.
5. **Confirm the aircraft is not on a Part 121/135 CAMP.** If it is, the § 65.95(a)(1) privilege does not apply.
6. **Inspect personally.** No delegation of the inspection.
7. **Inspect for conformity and workmanship** per § 43.13: methods/techniques/practices, materials of suitable quality, condition at least equal to original or properly altered condition.
8. **Check compatibility** with prior repairs and alterations, structural interactions, load paths, systems separation, and clearance.
9. **Check weight and balance, operating limitations, placards, and AFM/ AFM supplement revisions** required by the alteration; confirm the aircraft documents reflect them.
10. **Check continued airworthiness items:** instructions for continued airworthiness, inspection program impact, AD status, and any new life limits or inspection requirements.
11. **Record:** execute **FAA Form 337** for the major repair/alteration per **§ 43.9(d)**, and make the § 43.9(a)–(c) maintenance record entries (description, date, signature, certificate number).
12. **Approve for return to service** per § 43.5 and § 43.7(b), then ensure the operator's records reflect the current status of required major alterations (§ 91.417).
13. **Maintain your own qualification:** keep the IA current under § 65.92/§ 65.93, and notify the responsible office if your fixed base of operations changes.

**Open interpretive point (flag, do not assert):** whether an IA who personally performed the alteration may then inspect and approve that same alteration for return to service is a question on which FAA field guidance has been applied narrowly in practice. Confirm the current FAA position with the responsible FSDO before relying on self-approval in an alteration workflow.

---

## 9. Mapping to the "FAA-AMT" context

- **AMT** = Aviation Maintenance Technician. The AMT certificates (airframe, powerplant, or both) are issued under 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart B; the Airman Certification Standards for AMTs govern the mechanic knowledge/practical/oral tests.
- **IA is a separate authorization**, not an AMT rating. Its eligibility path is § 65.91, and its test (§ 65.91(c)(5)) is expressly built around **returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and around annual/progressive inspections.
- **Training-and-testing implication:** an AMT-track curriculum that touches major alterations should treat three things as distinct: (a) *performing* the alteration (mechanic privilege, § 65.81/§ 65.3), (b) *approving the data* (Administrator/designee/STC — never the IA), and (c) *approving for return to service* (§ 43.7(b), § 65.85 for rating-limited A&P sign-off, § 65.95(a)(1) for the IA). The most common instructional error is collapsing (b) into (c).
- **Study sources:** FAA IA Information Guide (current edition), AC 65-30 (IA guidance), AC 43-210A (field approval of major repair/alteration data), AC 20-62E (eligibility/approved parts), and the FAA's IA knowledge-test question bank and IA test guide. These are guidance/interpretation; the regulation itself is the eCFR text of Parts 1, 43, 65, and 91.

---

## 10. Citation table for the deliverable

| Proposition | Citation |

| IA eligibility (5 conditions, incl. 3-year A&P tenure, 3-year active engagement, fixed base, equipment/facilities/data, written test on major repairs/alterations) | 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5) |

| IA may perform annual / perform or supervise progressive inspection | 14 CFR 65.95(a)(2) |
| IA cannot approve the data; must personally perform the inspection; no delegation | FAA IA Information Guide; AC 65-30B |
| A&P with airframe or powerplant rating may approve for return to service after major repair/alteration within rating, per approved data | 14 CFR 65.85 |
| Approval for return to service; persons authorized | 14 CFR 43.5; 43.7(b) |
| FAA Form 337 required for major repair/alteration | 14 CFR 43.9(d) |
| Work must be done per approved data and to at least original/properly altered condition | 14 CFR 43.13(a), (b) |
| Definition of major alteration | 14 CFR 1.1 |
| List of major alterations / major repairs | 14 CFR Part 43, App. A / App. B |
| Field approval procedure for major repair/alteration data | AC 43-210A (current revision) |
| Operator records showing current status of required major alterations | 14 CFR 91.417 |

---

## 11. Verification actions before publication

1. Open each eCFR section link in §2 and confirm the paragraph letters and the amendment level shown on the Details tab.
2. Replace every *[paraphrase — confirm wording]* marker with the verbatim eCFR text, or leave the paraphrase and drop the quotation framing.
3. Confirm the current revision letter of AC 43-210 and AC 65-30, and the current edition of the FAA IA Information Guide.
4. Confirm with the responsible FSDO the open interpretive point in §8 (self-approval after performing an alteration).
5. Record the eCFR retrieval date in the document footer; regulatory text is point-in-time and this answer should be re-verified at each IA renewal cycle (the odd-numbered-year March 31 boundary is a natural review trigger).
